quests.sentence: The new policy which nobody had read carefully yet took effect on Monday
quests.correctAnswer: The new policy-which nobody had read carefully yet-took effect on Monday.
quests.hint: Em dashes can replace commas around a parenthetical to add stronger emphasis.
quests.explanation: Em dashes (-) can enclose a non-essential clause to make it stand out more dramatically than commas would. They replace the commas around 'which nobody had read carefully yet.'

quests.sentence: Three colleagues her oldest friends at the firm attended the farewell party
quests.correctAnswer: Three colleagues-her oldest friends at the firm-attended the farewell party.
quests.hint: The appositive here deserves special emphasis - use em dashes instead of commas.
quests.explanation: Em dashes around an appositive or parenthetical phrase create stronger emphasis than commas. Both dashes replace the pair of commas.

quests.sentence: The chef's signature dish a slow-roasted lamb shank sold out within an hour
quests.correctAnswer: The chef's signature dish-a slow-roasted lamb shank-sold out within an hour.
quests.hint: The appositive 'a slow-roasted lamb shank' can be set off emphatically.
quests.explanation: Em dashes lend a dramatic or emphatic quality to an appositive or aside that commas would make feel routine.

quests.sentence: She opened the envelope and then she stopped
quests.correctAnswer: She opened the envelope-and then she stopped.
quests.hint: The narrative breaks sharply. Use an em dash to show the abrupt pause.
quests.explanation: An em dash can signal a sharp break in thought or narrative flow, often where a comma would be too gentle.

quests.sentence: I was just about to explain when suddenly the fire alarm went off
quests.correctAnswer: I was just about to explain-when suddenly the fire alarm went off.
quests.hint: The explanation is cut short by a sudden event - show that break.
quests.explanation: An em dash before an unexpected interruption shows a sudden break in the speaker's intended action or thought.

quests.sentence: He was about to announce the winner and then the lights went out
quests.correctAnswer: He was about to announce the winner-and then the lights went out.
quests.hint: The lights going out is a dramatic, sudden interruption of the planned announcement.
quests.explanation: An em dash before 'and then' heightens dramatic tension when one event abruptly cuts off another.

quests.sentence: The report see Appendix B shows a 12% increase in sales
quests.correctAnswer: The report (see Appendix B) shows a 12% increase in sales.
quests.hint: References to other sections belong in parentheses as supplementary information.
quests.explanation: Parentheses enclose information that is supplementary - useful but not essential to the sentence. References like 'see Appendix B' are typical uses.

quests.sentence: The annual fee currently $120 will increase next January
quests.correctAnswer: The annual fee (currently $120) will increase next January.
quests.hint: The current price is bonus detail, not the main point - use parentheses.
quests.explanation: Parentheses are used for incidental or clarifying information that the reader can skip without losing the core message.

quests.sentence: The medication take one tablet twice daily should be kept at room temperature
quests.correctAnswer: The medication (take one tablet twice daily) should be kept at room temperature.
quests.hint: The dosage instruction is parenthetical - it adds detail without changing the main statement.
quests.explanation: Short instructions or clarifications that supplement rather than define the subject can be enclosed in parentheses.

quests.sentence: The project was delayed by three months. see the timeline chart for details The board was informed immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The project was delayed by three months. (See the timeline chart for details.) The board was informed immediately.
quests.hint: When an entire sentence is inside parentheses, the period goes inside the closing mark.
quests.explanation: If a parenthetical is a complete sentence standing alone, it starts with a capital letter and its closing punctuation (period) goes inside the closing parenthesis.

quests.sentence: She completed the course with distinction. the exam required a score above 90% Her certificate arrived by post.
quests.correctAnswer: She completed the course with distinction. (The exam required a score above 90%.) Her certificate arrived by post.
quests.hint: The fact about the exam is a complete sentence added as a standalone aside.
quests.explanation: A standalone parenthetical sentence is capitalised and its period is placed inside the closing parenthesis, not after it.

quests.sentence: The renovation will take six weeks. please plan alternative arrangements and contact facilities if needed We apologise for the inconvenience.
quests.correctAnswer: The renovation will take six weeks. (Please plan alternative arrangements and contact facilities if needed.) We apologise for the inconvenience.
quests.hint: A complete instruction as a parenthetical aside needs capital letter and internal period.
quests.explanation: When parenthetical content is a full imperative sentence, capitalise the first word and place the full stop inside the closing parenthesis.

quests.sentence: The conference featured speakers from Paris, France, London, England, and Berlin, Germany
quests.correctAnswer: The conference featured speakers from Paris, France; London, England; and Berlin, Germany.
quests.hint: Each city–country pair already uses a comma - use semicolons to separate the list items.
quests.explanation: When list items contain internal commas, semicolons replace the usual commas between items to prevent confusion.

quests.sentence: We interviewed a nurse who works nights, a teacher who coaches sports, and a chef who grows his own vegetables
quests.correctAnswer: We interviewed a nurse who works nights; a teacher who coaches sports; and a chef who grows his own vegetables.
quests.hint: Each list item has a relative clause inside it - use semicolons between items.
quests.explanation: In a list where each item includes a relative clause (creating internal commas), semicolons are used between the list items for clarity.

quests.sentence: The package contained a red scarf, size medium, a blue hat, one size fits all, and grey gloves, extra large
quests.correctAnswer: The package contained a red scarf, size medium; a blue hat, one size fits all; and grey gloves, extra large.
quests.hint: Each item has a size description - use semicolons to separate the three main items.
quests.explanation: When every item in a list already has a comma for clarification, the items are separated by semicolons to keep the list readable.

quests.sentence: The principal opened the assembly with these words hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard
quests.correctAnswer: The principal opened the assembly with these words: "Hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard."
quests.hint: 'These words' signals that a formal quotation follows - use a colon before the quoted text.
quests.explanation: A colon is used before a formal or lengthy quotation introduced by a complete sentence. The first word of the quote is capitalised.

quests.sentence: Her note read as follows please return all borrowed equipment by Friday afternoon
quests.correctAnswer: Her note read as follows: "Please return all borrowed equipment by Friday afternoon."
quests.hint: 'Read as follows' sets up a formal citation - use a colon to introduce it.
quests.explanation: Phrases like 'read as follows' or 'stated as follows' signal a formal quotation introduced by a colon.

quests.sentence: The sign on the door said exactly this no entry without an appointment
quests.correctAnswer: The sign on the door said exactly this: "No entry without an appointment."
quests.hint: 'Said exactly this' explicitly introduces the sign's wording - a colon is appropriate.
quests.explanation: A colon introduces a quotation when the preceding clause explicitly says that exact words follow ('said exactly this,' 'as follows,' etc.).

quests.sentence: The CEO ended the memo with a clear directive all staff must complete the training by 31 March
quests.correctAnswer: The CEO ended the memo with a clear directive: all staff must complete the training by 31 March.
quests.hint: 'A clear directive' promises that what follows is the directive itself.
quests.explanation: A colon after a complete sentence introduces the specific information that the sentence promised - here, the directive itself.

quests.sentence: The warning label carried a single message keep away from open flames
quests.correctAnswer: The warning label carried a single message: keep away from open flames.
quests.hint: 'A single message' sets up what is coming - introduce it with the right mark.
quests.explanation: When a noun phrase like 'a single message' announces that specific wording follows, a colon introduces that wording.

quests.sentence: Her advice was always the same work hard be kind and never give up
quests.correctAnswer: Her advice was always the same: work hard, be kind, and never give up.
quests.hint: 'Always the same' signals that a specific list follows.
quests.explanation: A colon introduces the list that the preceding statement has announced. The three items in the list use serial commas.

quests.sentence: Although the weather was bad the hike which we had planned for months went ahead
quests.correctAnswer: Although the weather was bad, the hike-which we had planned for months-went ahead.
quests.hint: Comma after the introductory 'although' clause; em dashes for the emphatic 'which' aside.
quests.explanation: An introductory 'although' clause takes a comma, and the non-restrictive 'which' clause can be emphasised with em dashes instead of commas.

quests.sentence: Her first novel I finished it in one sitting became a bestseller and was adapted into a film
quests.correctAnswer: Her first novel-I finished it in one sitting-became a bestseller and was adapted into a film.
quests.hint: The personal aside 'I finished it in one sitting' is an emphatic interjection.
quests.explanation: Em dashes set off a strongly emphatic parenthetical that breaks into the sentence more forcefully than commas would.

quests.sentence: When the results finally came in 48 hours late the team celebrated with a dinner party and some well-deserved champagne
quests.correctAnswer: When the results finally came in-48 hours late-the team celebrated with a dinner party and some well-deserved champagne.
quests.hint: '48 hours late' is a sharp, emphatic aside inside the introductory clause.
quests.explanation: Em dashes can set off an emphatic aside even inside an introductory clause, provided the meaning remains clear.

quests.sentence: She had one rule in her kitchen never waste food
quests.correctAnswer: She had one rule in her kitchen: never waste food.
quests.hint: A colon introduces the rule that the sentence has promised.
quests.explanation: A colon follows a complete clause and introduces the specific information that clause announced - here, the one rule.

quests.sentence: Everything about that evening the food the music the company was perfect
quests.correctAnswer: Everything about that evening-the food, the music, the company-was perfect.
quests.hint: A list interrupts the sentence dramatically - em dashes around the list, commas within it.
quests.explanation: Em dashes can enclose a dramatic or emphatic list that interrupts a sentence. Commas still separate the items inside the list.

quests.sentence: The goal was simple get ten thousand followers by the end of the year
quests.correctAnswer: The goal was simple: get ten thousand followers by the end of the year.
quests.hint: 'Simple' announces that what follows is the simple goal.
quests.explanation: After an adjective that promises a definition or explanation, a colon is used to introduce that explanation.

quests.sentence: The manager who had worked here for fifteen years I believe announced her retirement at the all-staff meeting
quests.correctAnswer: The manager, who had worked here for fifteen years-I believe-announced her retirement at the all-staff meeting.
quests.hint: Two interruptions: a non-restrictive 'who' clause and an emphatic 'I believe' aside.
quests.explanation: Non-restrictive 'who' clauses take commas; an emphatic aside inside the clause can take em dashes for stronger separation.

quests.sentence: The three finalists a singer from Seoul a guitarist from Lagos and a pianist from Vienna performed brilliantly
quests.correctAnswer: The three finalists-a singer from Seoul, a guitarist from Lagos, and a pianist from Vienna-performed brilliantly.
quests.hint: The list of finalists interrupts the sentence dramatically - em dashes around the list.
quests.explanation: A list that interrupts a main clause for dramatic effect is enclosed in em dashes. Commas within the list still separate the items.

quests.sentence: Although she doubted herself to be fair everyone else did too she delivered the keynote address with complete confidence
quests.correctAnswer: Although she doubted herself-to be fair, everyone else did too-she delivered the keynote address with complete confidence.
quests.hint: Two things: comma after the introductory 'although' clause, and em dashes around the emphatic aside.
quests.explanation: Introductory subordinate clauses can have an emphatic parenthetical inside them, set off by em dashes. The main clause follows the closing em dash.
